sub_agendas_items.title: CSC-2026-06 –  Greenbank Park
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor W. Lo:
Greenbank Park, at 895 Greenbank Road, is a small community park with play structures, a swing set, and a splash pad, popular among local families. The park has chain link fencing along its Greenbank Road frontage.
Most park users enter from the neighbourhood via Fieldgate and Knollsbrook drives, but the winter-maintained pathways are important connectors for the neighbourhood east of Greenbank Road with shops, clinics, recreation, schools, and other neighbourhoods west of Greenbank Road. As such, the park includes an important access point from Greenbank Road via an opening in the fence.
However, that access means the swing set is just about 30 metres from the edge of Greenbank Road via the pathway, while one of the play structures is just 50 metres away. While parents and caregivers are reasonably expected to watch over their children, circumstances may divert their attention for just the wrong amount of time.

sub_agendas_items.title: CSC-2026-07 – Artificial pitch rentals for recreational cricket
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor D. Hill:
Ottawa is currently in the process of doubling the number of City-operated cricket pitches. However, there is still a gap in park capacity for recreational cricket players who do not require a high-quality pitch and field to play, and must compete with organized leagues to rent the limited number of fields with pitches installed. 
To accommodate recreational players, would it be feasible for the city to purchase 2 to 5 artificial mats/pitches and allow recreational clubs to rent those pitches at the same time that they rent a sports field for play (such as a soccer or ultimate frisbee field)? 
What would be the benefits of such a program? 
What would be the limitations and liabilities? 
How much would such a program cost?
